title: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi scripts history, creates world record at just 15

Sooryavanshi was the leading run-scorer with 151 runs across three innings. He scored a match-winning 81 runs in the final T20I match. This award followed a challenging series for the young cricketer in England.

Gandhi questioned Prime Minister Modi's promises regarding student FIRs. He stated that pellet guns were fired at students in Delhi. The Congress leader demanded an apology and action against attackers.

title: Jeff Bezos ex-wife MacKenzie Scott helped write a 'donation playbook' for Snap founder
content: Snap co-founder Evan Spiegel and Miranda Kerr have donated $550 million to erase medical debt. This significant contribution will benefit over 261,000 Californians facing financial hardship.  The donation follows a model pioneered by MacKenzie Scott, who has given billions to nonprofits.  The funds will be channeled through Undue Medical Debt, a prominent organization.  This initiative targets vulnerable residents, alleviating burdens of unpayable medical bills.

title: Baby goat jumps, freezes and topples due to inherited muscle condition
content: Fainting goats do not actually faint. Also known as myotonic goats, they have a rare inherited muscle condition called myotonia congenita that causes their muscles to become temporarily stiff when they are startled. The breed is valued for its heavy muscling, meat production, strong maternal instincts and ability to thrive on forage-based farming, making it much more than its unusual behaviour.

title: Church and Jesus statue caught in Trump’s border wall land fight
content: The US government seeks land for a border wall near Mount Cristo Rey. This sacred site is a pilgrimage destination for thousands of faithful people. The Roman Catholic Diocese of Las Cruces opposes the land acquisition and wall construction. Church officials argue the wall infringes upon religious freedom and desecrates the holy place. A legal battle is underway as the government pursues eminent domain for the project.

title: 'Silicon Valley came after my people': Google AI CEO on why DeepMind sold to Google
content: Google DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis has explained why he sold DeepMind to Google in 2014. Competing with Big Tech needed $7 billion, he says, while he could barely raise $10 million rounds. The Atari breakthrough put DeepMind on Silicon Valley's radar, and rivals began offering his researchers $10 million a year. With no product and no revenue, Hassabis took Larry Page's roughly $650 million offer.

title: Hubble discovers four hidden stars just 65 light-years from Earth, unseen until now
content: Astronomers have confirmed four hidden white dwarfs orbiting nearby red dwarf stars.  Ultraviolet observations from the Hubble Space Telescope enabled this significant detection.  These stellar remnants were previously concealed by their brighter companion stars.  The findings refine estimates of the local white dwarf population.  This discovery offers new insights into binary star system evolution.

title: 16 years after Cochin Haneefa's death, family moves into dream home; Dileep attends
content: Today, "Cochin Haneefa's A.B. Manzil" stands as more than just a house. It represents the fulfilment of a dream, the resilience of a family that overcame years of hardship, and a lasting tribute to an actor whose timeless performances continue to bring joy to Malayalam cinema audiences.

title: 'Get down, get down': Seattle food festival shooting caught on livestream; 2 killed, 5 injured

Investigations into the motive and any other suspects are ongoing.

title: Wildfires in Spain and France force nearly three lakh to evacuate

In France, firefighters are working tirelessly to contain the fire's advance toward Bordeaux. Meanwhile, Spain faces its largest wildfire with destruction exceeding 50,000 hectares since January, prompting the European Union to provide aid. Spanish Prime Minister Sanchez plans to announce a civil protection emergency for the central provinces impacted.

title: APJ Abdul Kalam's legacy lives on in India's missiles, space programme

Kalam's work at DRDO and ISRO expanded national strategic autonomy. His vision also guided technology development for a developed India. The nation honors his role in building scientific and defense strength.

title: JNU scholar Neha Bora: How a 23-day hunger strike sparked a movement
content: JNU research scholar Neha Bora emerged as a prominent face of a student movement after leading a 23-day hunger strike at Delhi’s Jantar Mantar. Her speeches, organisational role and commitment to students’ concerns brought nationwide attention through social media. The article explores her academic background, activism, public communication skills and the broader role of universities in shaping student leadership, while presenting her evolving journey without endorsing or opposing the movement.

title: How Lantana camara became one of India's worst invasive plants
content: Lantana camara, an ornamental shrub native to the Americas, has rapidly spread within India, now occupying more than forty percent of the country's tiger habitats. This resilient plant aggressively competes with native flora for essential resources. Increased forest degradation and human activity further fuel its proliferation, creating a troubling cycle. Efforts to eradicate this invasive species are both slow and expensive, leaving many forest areas vulnerable to future invasions.
